messages:
jonathan: quick proposal — add a per-tenant "allow_overflow" flag and a consent timestamp so Dedicated can 'escape' to Hosted for bursts when tenants opt in. thinking console + API + audit logs. thoughts?
rachel: hmm we need to be explicit about data residency and SLA differences. tenants in EEA might never be allowed to overflow to hosted in other regions. also billing implications. :thinking:
maya: agree with rachel. UX note: in the Console rollout I think this should be a toggle with three states: opt-in, opt-out, org-default. show which requests actually used overflow in the last 24h.
jonathan: yeah was imagining something like that. API param idea (draft):
```json
{"routing_policy": {"prefer": "dedicated", "fallback": "hosted", "consent_required": true, "consent_ts": "2026-03-10T15:02:00Z"}}
```
alex: small nit — we need to differentiate "consent" vs "compatibility". consent == tenant allowed data to go to hosted; compatibility == model variant available with same semantics (quantization/llm-arch). both must pass.
ops-ana: from an ops perspective we need an immutable audit trail: who toggled allow_overflow, when, and the trace IDs for any overflowed request. also add a metric `tenant.overflow.success` and `tenant.overflow.rejected` (for policy/compatibility failures).
maya: console wire idea: show per-model variant compatibility score & last-run evals next to the toggle. clickable "why rejected" that links to the eval diff. reduces support churn.
jonathan: good. question on enforcement: do we block at edge (403) if tenant is strict, or do we route then redact? prefer hard deny for strict data tenants.
rachel: hard deny. anything else is a compliance risk. if they opt-in we can show a clear banner in console: "Requests may leave your dedicated pool and be served by hosted infra" with billing delta.
alex: rollout plan: expose API+console behind a feature flag, default false for tenants with sensitive tags, then canary to 5% of traffic for non-sensitive tenants. telemetry gating: require no errors and <1% identity-mismatch in first 24h before 100% rollout.
jonathan: agree. for telemetry — add a sample event payload we can use in the pipeline:
```text
{ event: "overflow_decision", tenant: "acme", decision: "hosted", reason: "capacity", trace_id: ".." }
```
ops-ana: also record model_variant source (e.g., redwood-v2-xxq8) and a field `data_plane_region` so auditors can prove residency.
deploy-bot: canary rollout for "tenant-overflow-refactor" started at 2167894300 — 5% non-sensitive traffic. monitor: infra-alert, billing-anomalies, eval-regressions.
jonathan: thanks — i'll get a PR up for API schema + console mocks. leaving a checklist here: 1) API schema + validation, 2) console toggle states & banners, 3) telemetry events + dashboards, 4) audit log retention, 5) canary plan + gates. anyone want to add items?
ops-ana: add: encryption-in-transit proof and KMS audit for hosted path.
rachel: add: contract/legal review for SLA/billing language.
maya: add: "why rejected" UX links to exact eval diff + prompt example.
alex: add: migration script to mark existing tenants default=false if they have sensitive tags.
jonathan: perfect, i'll post the PR and ping infra for the telemetry pipeline changes. :thumbsup:
